content:
While this week's focus has been on the iOS 27 public beta, Apple has simultaneously rolled out a new public beta firmware update for AirPods. This update finally brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: a custom equalizer.

AirPods Public Beta Details

The AirPods public beta firmware is version 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models are eligible to update:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 (Active Noise Cancellation)
  • AirPods Max 2

You can enroll in the AirPods public beta program through the Settings app on your iPhone. Once your AirPods are connected, you'll see a toggle in the Settings app to enable the beta firmware. After that, as long as the AirPods are in their charging case and within range of a paired iPhone, the beta will automatically download and install.

  • Open the Settings app
  • Tap on Bluetooth
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and enable AirPods Beta Updates

Custom Equalizer Lands on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, a long-awaited new feature will appear in the Settings app: a custom equalizer.

With the new custom equalizer controls, you can fine-tune the sound of your AirPods with greater precision. In the Settings app, you can adjust the AirPods' bass, mids, and treble.

Apple notes: "AirPods are designed and made by Apple to faithfully reproduce the sound of music, TV shows, movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can also customize how your AirPods perform when playing any audio."

When adjusting the custom equalizer, you can play songs from Apple Music directly in the Settings app to hear the effects of your adjustments in real time.

This is by no means the most professional equalizer feature on the market—just a basic three-band adjustment. However, for AirPods users, this is a long-awaited feature, and Apple has finally relented and made it available to everyone—though most people will probably stick with the default settings.

You can find the new custom equalizer feature under the Audio & Routing menu in your AirPods settings within the Settings app. This feature is available on all AirPods equipped with the H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other New Features iOS 27 Brings to AirPods

Here are the other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned Settings App: iOS 27 has redesigned the AirPods interface within the Settings app, organizing various controls into categories such as Hearing Health, Find My, Live Translation, and more.
  • Adaptive Audio Slider: The Settings app now includes a slider for more granular control over Adaptive Audio mode.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for several years, it has always required an Apple Watch to use. As my colleague Zac noted, iOS 27 brings the complete GymKit experience to the iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use the Find My app on your Apple Watch to precision-find your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a supported iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrap-Up

Which new AirPods feature are you most excited to try? Will you experiment with the new custom equalizer? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
